publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
bibl.publisher: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We propose a new framework for estimating generative models via an adversarial process, in which we simultaneously train two models: a generative model G that captures the data distribution, and a discriminative model D that estimates the probability that a sample came from the training data rather than G.

span.label: adversarial training of generative models
span.quote: In the proposed adversarial nets framework, the generative model is pitted against an adversary: a discriminative model that learns to determine whether a sample is from the model distribution or the data distribution.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We propose a new generative model estimation procedure that sidesteps these difficulties.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: adversarial training: a generator and discriminator compete in a minimax game - the generator learns to produce samples that fool the discriminator (which learns real vs fake), driving the generator toward the data distribution
span.quote: The generative model can be thought of as analogous to a team of counterfeiters, trying to produce fake currency and use it without detection, while the discriminative model is analogous to the police, trying to detect the counterfeit currency

span.label: the likelihood-estimation method has high variance and does not perform well in high dimensions
span.note: what this limits: the reported likelihood numbers: the estimation method DOES NOT PERFORM WELL IN HIGH DIMENSIONAL SPACES
span.quote: does not perform well in high dimensional spaces

span.label: The model gives no explicit representation of the generator's density, and the discriminator must be kept synchronised with the generator or the generator collapses (the 'Helvetica scenario').
span.note: what this limits: any use requiring a density or stable training: THERE IS NO EXPLICIT REPRESENTATION OF pg(x), AND D MUST BE SYNCHRONIZED WELL WITH G DURING TRAINING
span.quote: The disadvantages are primarily that there is no explicit representation of pg(x), and that D must be synchronized well with G during training (in particular, G must not be trained too much without updating D, in order to avoid “the Helvetica scenario” in which G collapses too many values of z to the same value of x to have enough diversity to model pdata), much as the negative chains of a Boltzmann machine must be kept up to date between learning steps.

span.label: The Parzen-window likelihood estimate used to evaluate the model is high-variance and performs poorly in high dimensions.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0, with the reason it was used anyway: IT HAS SOMEWHAT HIGH VARIANCE AND DOES NOT PERFORM WELL IN HIGH DIMENSIONAL SPACES BUT IT IS THE BEST METHOD AVAILABLE TO OUR KNOWLEDGE
span.quote: This method of estimating the likelihood has somewhat high variance and does not perform well in high dimensional spaces but it is the best method available to our knowledge.

span.label: The convergence result is proved in the non-parametric limit; using a multilayer perceptron for G breaks the theoretical guarantee.
span.note: what this limits: the convergence guarantee, which is proved in the non-parametric limit and does not cover the implementation: USING A MULTILAYER PERCEPTRON TO DEFINE G INTRODUCES MULTIPLE CRITICAL POINTS IN PARAMETER SPACE
span.quote: Using a multilayer perceptron to define G introduces multiple critical points in parameter space.

span.label: The authors do not claim the generated samples are better than those of existing methods.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison with existing generative models: WHILE WE MAKE NO CLAIM THAT THESE SAMPLES ARE BETTER THAN SAMPLES GENERATED BY EXISTING METHODS, WE BELIEVE THAT THESE SAMPLES ARE AT LEAST COMPETITIVE
span.quote: While we make no claim that these samples are better than samples generated by existing methods, we believe that these samples are at least competitive with the better generative models in the literature and highlight the potential of the adversarial framework.

span.label: The authors state their evaluation method is high-variance and poor in high dimensions, call it the best available, and report the paper's headline numbers on it.
span.note: what this limits: the log-likelihood figures in Table 1: they come from Gaussian Parzen-window estimation, which the authors say has somewhat high variance and does not perform well in high dimensional spaces
span.quote: This method of estimating the likelihood has somewhat high variance and does not perform well in high dimensional spaces but it is the best method available to our knowledge

span.label: The convergence results are proved in the non-parametric limit, and the paper states the implementation does not satisfy that condition and has no theoretical guarantee.
span.note: what this limits: the guarantee that pg converges to pdata: it is proved in a non-parametric setting, while the implementation optimises the parameters of a multilayer perceptron, which the paper says lacks theoretical guarantees
span.quote: In practice, adversarial nets represent a limited family of pg distributions via the function G(z; θg), and we optimize θg rather than pg itself. Using a multilayer perceptron to define G introduces multiple critical points in parameter space. However, the excellent performance of multilayer perceptrons in practice suggests that they are a reasonable model to use despite their lack of theoretical guarantees

span.label: The objective that is trained is not the objective that is analysed; the substitution is made because the analysed one saturates, and the equivalence claimed is of fixed points only.
span.note: what this limits: the relation between Eq. 1 and what was run: G is trained to maximize log D(G(z)) instead, which the paper says gives the same fixed point but much stronger gradients early in learning
span.quote: Rather than training G to minimize log(1 − D(G(z))) we can train G to maximize log D(G(z)). This objective function results in the same fixed point of the dynamics of G and D but provides much stronger gradients early in learning

span.label: The two stated disadvantages are structural, not incidental: the model has no explicit density, and training can collapse to too few outputs if the two networks fall out of step.
span.note: what this limits: adversarial nets as a density model or as a stable training procedure: there is no explicit representation of pg(x), and D must be synchronized well with G to avoid G collapsing too many values of z to the same value of x
span.quote: The disadvantages are primarily that there is no explicit representation of pg(x), and that D must be synchronized well with G during training (in particular, G must not be trained too much without updating D, in order to avoid “the Helvetica scenario” in which G collapses too many values of z to the same value of x to have enough diversity to model pdata), much as the negative chains of a Boltzmann machine must be kept up to date between learning steps

span.label: The claim made for the sample quality is a stated belief, and the paper explicitly declines to claim the samples are better than existing methods.
span.note: what this limits: the figures of generated samples as evidence of quality: the authors make no claim that they are better than existing methods and state only a belief that they are at least competitive
span.quote: While we make no claim that these samples are better than samples generated by existing methods, we believe that these samples are at least competitive with the better generative models in the literature and highlight the potential of the adversarial framework

span.label: a minimax two-player game between a generator and a discriminator, adapting game-theoretic adversarial competition to train generative models
span.quote: This framework corresponds to a minimax two-player game

span.label: the displayed samples declared to be FAIR RANDOM DRAWS rather than selected
span.note: eliminates: selection of the best outputs as the basis for judging the model - a figure of hand-picked samples shows what the model CAN do at its best, which is not what the distribution looks like, and nothing in the image itself would reveal the difference
span.quote: Samples are fair random draws, not cherry-picked.

span.label: a column showing the NEAREST TRAINING EXAMPLE beside each generated sample
span.note: eliminates: memorisation of the training set as the explanation of sample quality - a model that reproduced its training data would look excellent by every visual measure, and the neighbour column is what makes that checkable by the reader
span.quote: Rightmost column shows the nearest training example of the neighboring sample, in order to demonstrate that the model has not memorized the training set.

span.label: discriminator
span.quote: The number of steps to apply to the discriminator, k, is a hyperparameter

span.label: minimax game
span.quote: D and G play the following two-player minimax game with value function

span.label: adversarial nets
span.quote: We refer to this special case as adversarial nets

span.label: Parzen window
span.quote: by fitting a Gaussian Parzen window to the samples generated with G

span.label: log-likelihood
span.quote: and reporting the log-likelihood under this distribution

span.label: the training objective - AS ANALYSED vs AS TRAINED: the minimax value function of Eq. 1 is what the theorems are about; the implementation maximises a different function with the same fixed point, because the analysed one saturates early in learning
span.quote: This objective function results in the same fixed point of the dynamics of G and D but provides much stronger gradients early in learning

span.label: log-likelihood - AS A PARZEN-WINDOW ESTIMATE: not computed from the model, but from a Gaussian fitted to samples drawn from it, because the model has no tractable density
span.quote: We estimate probability of the test set data under pg by fitting a Gaussian Parzen window to the samples generated with G and reporting the log-likelihood under this distribution

span.label: adversarial nets - THE PAPER'S OWN NAME, and it names the special case, not the framework: the framework is general and 'adversarial nets' is what the authors call the multilayer-perceptron instance of it
span.quote: We refer to this special case as adversarial nets

span.label: the failure mode - NAMED AS A JOKE: 'the Helvetica scenario', in which the generator maps too many inputs to the same output; the field later renamed this mode collapse, and Table 2 records it as the single word Helvetica
span.quote: in particular, G must not be trained too much without updating D, in order to avoid “the Helvetica scenario” in which G collapses too many values of z to the same value of x to have enough diversity to model pdata

span.label: builds-on → game theory (minimax two-player game)
span.quote: This framework corresponds to a minimax two-player game

span.label: builds-on → SML/PCD training [31, 29]
span.quote: This strategy is analogous to the way that SML/PCD [31, 29] training maintains samples from a Markov chain from one learning step to the next in order to avoid burning in a Markov chain as part of the inner loop of learning.

span.label: builds-on → the Parzen-window likelihood evaluation procedure of Breuleux et al. [8]
span.quote: This procedure was introduced in Breuleux et al. [8] and used for various generative models for which the exact likelihood is not tractable [25, 3, 5].

span.label: extends → the generative stochastic network (GSN) framework [5]
span.quote: Compared to GSNs, the adversarial nets framework does not require a Markov chain for sampling.

span.label: extends → noise-contrastive estimation (NCE) [13]
span.quote: However, rather than fitting a separate discriminative model, the generative model itself is used to discriminate generated data from samples a fixed noise distribution.

span.label: log-likelihood —operationalised-as→ Parzen window
span.quote: We estimate probability of the test set data under pg by fitting a Gaussian Parzen window to the samples generated with G and reporting the log-likelihood under this distribution

span.label: adversarial nets —operationalised-as→ minimax game
span.quote: D and G play the following two-player minimax game with value function

span.label: D = 1/2 — discriminator output at the optimal solution (cannot distinguish real from fake)
span.quote: a unique solution exists, with G recovering the training data distribution and D equal to 1 2 everywhere

span.label: At the unique optimum, G recovers the true data distribution and D outputs 1/2 everywhere; with MLPs the whole system trains by backpropagation, needing no Markov chains or unrolled inference.
span.quote: a unique solution exists, with G recovering the training data distribution and D equal to 1 2 everywhere. In the case where G and D are defined by multilayer perceptrons, the entire system can be trained with backpropagation.

span.label: generator vs discriminator adversarial training
span.quote: we simultaneously train two models: a generative model G that captures the data distribution, and a discriminative model D

span.label: generated-sample realism / distribution match
span.quote: with G recovering the training data distribution and D equal to 1 2 everywhere

span.label: generative adversarial net (minimax game)
span.quote: This framework corresponds to a minimax two-player game

span.label: discriminator D
span.quote: a discriminative model D that estimates the probability that a sample came from the training data rather than G

span.label: Bayesian
span.quote: More recent examples of training a generative machine by back-propagating into it include recent work on auto-encoding variational Bayes [20] and stochastic backpropagation [24].

span.label: standard-error
span.note: about this quote: QUOTE REPAIRED (Q-697): the extractor split a hyphen-space and the quote was recorded faithfully with the damage in it, which made it unanchorable. The repaired string is an EXACT SUBSTRING of the staged text - that is why it was accepted, not because a rule produced it. The text as originally recorded is kept in `evidence_as_extracted`.
span.quote: The reported numbers on MNIST are the mean loglikelihood of samples on test set, with the standard error of the mean computed across examples.

span.label: variance
span.quote: This method of estimating the likelihood has somewhat high variance and does not perform well in high dimensional spaces but it is the best method available to our knowledge.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2661.
